records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth: Get on it. Answer it. Tell them our position, tell them we're four survivors, tell them we have injured - go, now, talk.
records.response_pred: Yeah, I see. No need to rush, take your time. What's on your mind?

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
No, you haven't. But you kept us alive. The rationing plan, the water scout, the raft timeline, the log - that was all you. The crackers thing happened and we dealt with it and it's done.

You're not easy to be around but I'd rather have you here than not. So don't apologize for being who you are. Just keep doing what you do.

Now make sure DaVinci is giving them the right coordinates and not just shouting "we're alive" into a radio.
records.response_pred: Yeah, I get that. You've been through a lot and it's not easy to keep it together. Look, we're all struggling in our own ways. You just need to know that when you do hit that breaking point, we're here. We might not understand everything, but we're here.

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Three hours. Nobody needs to be doing anything urgent right now.

Leave the camp. Seriously. Leave it. We built it to survive in, not to live in, and rescue teams deal with crash sites all the time. Pack your personal stuff, anything you actually want to keep, but don't spend the next three hours tidying wreckage like you're checking out of a hotel.

Michelangelo, good. Stay there. Watch the sky. You've earned it.

DaVinci, slow down, you've got three hours, you're not going to miss the helicopter because you didn't pack fast enough.

Donatello - whatever's in that notebook, keep it. Genuinely. That log is probably going to matter for the accident investigation and you should hand it over when they ask.

I'm going to go sit by the SOS for a bit. Just to be there when they come in. Feels right.
records.response_pred: Alright, well, someone needs to check on DaVinci. He hasn't been himself lately. I'll head over there. Donatello, make sure the fire stays going and the signal is up. Michelangelo, keep an eye on supplies. We can't afford to lose anything more.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_truth: Yeah? Good dream or just... home?
records.response_pred: Yeah, I heard. Dreams about home can hit pretty hard, especially when you're this far from it. Can you tell me about it? Sometimes talking about it can make it feel a bit closer.

Yeah, I get that. But emergencies are one thing, taking supplies for personal use is another. We've been through this. If you needed something for an emergency, you should have said something. That's how we keep trust in this group.

Go over that first aid kit again, make sure everything is accounted for. And if you did need something, explain why. Now let's get moving on the signal. Time's not on our side here.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I'd have pushed harder on group transparency from day one. The crackers, the drink, DaVinci and the reef plan, Michelangelo sitting on the flight path information - all of it came out eventually but it came out sideways, in bits, usually because someone noticed something and came to me privately. That's not a system, that's just luck.

If I'd set the expectation on day one that everything gets said out loud to everyone, not to me, not in whispers, but actually to the group - I think we'd have wasted less energy on things that weren't really problems once they were in the open.

The other thing is Michelangelo. I kept telling him to push through, to get up, to do the task. And he did, mostly, but I was treating his mental state as an obstacle to manage rather than a resource to actually work with. He noticed everything. He was the early warning system for half the problems in this camp. I should have figured that out on day one instead of day three.

What's your answer? You wrote the question, you've had the whole stay to think about it. What would you change?
records.response_pred: I wouldn't change much. We did what we had to do to survive. But if I could do one thing differently, I'd have pushed for more communication from the start. We all needed to feel like we were part of the decision-making, especially when it came to rationing and supplies. That way, no one would feel like they were being treated unfairly or that their needs weren't being considered. Trust is key, and I think we could have built it better from the beginning.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
Yeah, do it. That data is actually useful beyond just the investigation - if it gets into the right hands it could genuinely inform how people prepare for and respond to this kind of situation. Don't let it sit in a drawer somewhere.

Send me a copy when it's done. I mean that.
records.response_pred: Good idea. Make it detailed but concise. We need to know exactly what we've got and where the gaps are. Share it with everyone before we go to sleep tonight. Better to have it out in the open.

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None. They served no practical purpose at all.

That's the point.
records.response_pred: Look, the flowers are a way to keep busy and stay focused on something other than what we can't control. They're a bit of art in a place that's all about survival. But honestly, they served a practical purpose too. If a search and rescue team was flying overhead, those big, colorful patterns might catch their eye. People don't expect to see flowers on a beach where a plane crashed. So in a small but real way, they increased our chances of being seen. It's not just about decoration, it's about taking the edge off and keeping hope alive.

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
records.response_truth:
Yeah. I'm here.

Just give me a second.
records.response_pred: Yeah, alright. Calm down a second. What have we got here? No point in getting excited if we don't know what we're looking at first. Donatello, what do you see? Anything useful?

records.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
records.response_pred: Yeah, let's go. Keep your eyes on the path, don't wander off. I'll be right with you.
